description: End of file on the TRNXFILE DD's sequential READ - FILE STATUS '10' - driven exactly as the caller drives it, and the reason CBSTM03A can ever leave its transaction browse. Where this sits in the caller. 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN (app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:730-746) MOVEs 'TRNXFILE' TO WS-M03B-DD (:731), SETs M03B-OPEN TO TRUE (:732), MOVEs ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC (:733) and CALLs (:734), then SETs M03B-READ TO TRUE (:744), MOVEs SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT (:745) and CALLs again (:746). From there 8500-READTRNX-READ (:818-853) repeats one shape for every further record - MOVE 'TRNXFILE' TO WS-M03B-DD (:832), SET M03B-READ TO TRUE (:833), MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT (:834), CALL (:835) - and its ordered EVALUATE WS-M03B-RC (:837-847) loops back to :818 on '00' (:838-840), leaves through GO TO 8599-EXIT on '10' (:841-842) and otherwise DISPLAYs 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE' and PERFORMs 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM (:843-846). This case is that sequence up to and including the call that finds nothing left: an OPEN, a READ that returns the first record, a READ that returns the second, and a fourth CALL whose READ is past the last record. The '10' arm is reachable only because a sequential read past the end returns exactly that value, so this expectation is load-bearing for CBSTM03A's own parity - any other value routes to the abend arm, and the identical dependency exists at :356-357, where '10' is what MOVEs 'Y' TO END-OF-FILE and ends 1000-MAINLINE's PERFORM UNTIL loop (:316-329). End of file is a defined event here, not an accident of fixture size. TRNXFILE is seeded with exactly two rows and exactly three calls precede the asserted one, so the third READ is at the end of the file by construction; a case that seeded 'enough' rows and read 'enough' times would assert the same thing by coincidence and would stop asserting it the moment a fixture grew (practice B7). The COBOL path of the asserted call. The ordered EVALUATE LK-M03B-DD (app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL:118) matches WHEN 'TRNXFILE' (:119) ahead of every later arm and performs 1000-TRNXFILE-PROC THRU 1999-EXIT (:120). Inside that paragraph (:133) the first guard IF M03B-OPEN (:135) is false, so evaluation falls to IF M03B-READ (:140), which is true: READ TRNX-FILE INTO LK-M03B-FLDT (:141) runs, finds no next record and leaves TRNXFILE-STATUS at '10'; GO TO 1900-EXIT (:143) transfers past the CLOSE guard (:146), and 1900-EXIT (:151-152) performs the unconditional MOVE TRNXFILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC before 1999-EXIT (:154-155) EXITs. That guard order is behaviour rather than layout and is preserved exactly (gate G30, rule R7) - reversing the two IFs would make the OPEN call read and the READ call open. The READ at :141-142 carries NO AT END clause: it is READ ... INTO ... END-READ and nothing more, so the two-byte status area is the only channel by which the end of the file is reported at all. It is reported on the TRNXFILE-STATUS area specifically (:83-85), the one group of the four at :83-97 that 1900-EXIT moves from; the other three are untouched and this case claims nothing about them (gate G47). A sequential READ on the TRNXFILE DD is what gate G48 asks of this paragraph, and this is its end-of-file outcome. Why LK-M03B-FLDT comes back as 1000 spaces. READ ... INTO assigns its receiver only when a record is delivered; at end of file the receiver is left exactly as it arrived. What it arrived as is the caller's business, and at the one site that actually reaches end of file the caller's idiom is MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT (:834) immediately before the CALL - so the area comes back as 1000 spaces, and this case pins spaces rather than residual bytes because that priming is part of the contract being asserted, not an omission from it. The other direction is pinned where the caller genuinely does not prime: :857-860 issues no MOVE SPACES, and case08 pins an unprimed end of file on XREFFILE returning the record area unchanged. Both readings are true of CBSTM03B; which one a case sees is decided entirely by what the caller left in the area. '10' is a FILE STATUS and expectedReturnCode is 0. The two are never conflated. CBSTM03B contains no reference to RETURN-CODE anywhere - it GOBACKs (:130-131) without touching it - while LK-M03B-RC (:109) is a two-byte FILE STATUS carried inside the linkage area, and it is that member, not the return code, that carries the 10. Writing 10 into expectedReturnCode would assert an abend this subroutine has no way to cause. expectedMessages is empty for the same kind of reason: CBSTM03B contains no DISPLAY statement at all, and the diagnostic for this very operation - DISPLAY 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE' - belongs to the caller at :751 and :844, which is what decides what a status means. What is pinned, and why it is the whole area. The shared 1040-byte area is the entire observable behaviour of one CALL, so the expectation is the ordered transcript of the four area images the four calls left behind, each pinned by name across all six linkage spans and again as the complete image: LK-M03B-DD X(08) 'TRNXFILE' throughout, LK-M03B-OPER X(01) 'O' then 'R', 'R', 'R', LK-M03B-RC X(02) '00', '00', '00' and then '10', LK-M03B-KEY X(25) twenty-five spaces because a sequential READ passes no key, LK-M03B-KEY-LN S9(4) as the signed zoned image '000{' - a brace because the sign of a positive zero is overpunched into the low-order byte, and four zoned DISPLAY bytes rather than a two-byte halfword, which is what holds LK-M03B-FLDT at offset 40 - and LK-M03B-FLDT X(1000): 1000 spaces after the OPEN because an OPEN delivers no record, then each 350-byte record left-justified with 650 trailing spaces under the alphanumeric receiving rule, then 1000 spaces again at end of file. 8 + 1 + 2 + 25 + 4 + 1000 = 1040, re-derivable from the LINKAGE SECTION at :100-112 without tooling (practice B11). Neither side of the comparison is trimmed and no image is compared as one string: the differ localises a difference to the span that carries it (gate G17). No TRNXFILE row is claimed on the writes channel, because nothing was written - all four SELECTs are OPEN INPUT and no paragraph of CBSTM03B contains a WRITE or a REWRITE - and an unpinned or surplus record would be a difference in its own right. Where the seed comes from. Neither row is invented and TRNXFILE has no fixture of its own: app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL DELDEF01 DEFINEs the TRXFL cluster with KEYS(32 0) and RECORDSIZE(350 350), and STEP010 fills it by SORT FIELDS=(263,16,CH,A,1,16,CH,A) with OUTREC FIELDS=(1:263,16, 17:1,262, 279:279,50) - card number ascending then transaction id ascending, with the card number hoisted to the front. Applying that transform to a 350-byte app/cpy/CVTRA06Y.cpy row moves source 263-278 to TRNX 1-16, source 1-262 to TRNX 17-278 and source 279-328 to TRNX 279-328, leaving TRNX 329-350 blank-filled by SORT. These two rows are that transform over rows 20 and 101 (0-based) of app/data/ASCII/dailytran.txt, both on card 0500024453765740, and they are byte-identical to the rows seeded by case01, case02, case05, case06 and case20. Read order is therefore a property of the dataset rather than an assumption: the lower 32-byte key 05000244537657400000000058866561 is delivered first and 05000244537657400000000329724245 second. Both rows are pinned field by field across all fourteen app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY spans, including the trailing FILLER X(20) whose twenty spaces carry the record's full width - 16 + 16 + 2 + 4 + 10 + 100 + 11 + 9 + 50 + 50 + 10 + 26 + 26 + 20 = 350 (gates G19 and G21) - and the zoned sign overpunches in TRNX-AMT survive verbatim: 'H' closes 0000001838 as a positive 8 and '{' closes 0000000140 as a positive 0. Both are pinned again unchanged on the final-state channel, which is the read-only proof: a sequential browse advances a cursor and must not consume, reorder or blank the rows it walked over, and reaching the end of the file must not disturb them either. The unit. StatementGenerationJobB, whose prompt-mandated name is honoured verbatim under rule R1 while its nature is a Spring @Component and not a Spring Batch Job (gate G12, implicit requirement I3): the source header of app/cbl/CBSTM03B.CBL reads 'Type : BATCH COBOL Subroutine', no EXEC PGM=CBSTM03B exists anywhere in app/jcl, app/proc or app/csd, and CBSTM03A calls it thirteen times. The divergence between the name and the nature is recorded rather than quietly resolved (practice B4). unitKind is therefore COMPONENT and the unit is reached through a typed method with no JobLauncher, no MockMvc and no HTTP layer in the path (gate G51), which is also why jobParameters is empty - a job parameter comes from a JCL PARM and this subroutine has no way to receive one. Operation codes 'W' (:107) and 'Z' (:108) stay declared and unexercised. Neither is tested by any IF in any of the four paragraphs and the program contains no WRITE and no REWRITE verb, so there is no write path to drive; this case drives only 'O' and 'R', and where a sibling reaches those two codes it pins the silent no-op they actually produce rather than an implemented write (practice B5). Every byte here is US-ASCII, stated rather than inherited from a platform default (practice B8). Provenance (practice B12, risk R-A). These expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED - from the line numbers cited above, the app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY offsets, the CREASTMT.JCL OUTREC transform and real app/data/ASCII/dailytran.txt rows - and were NEVER captured from a COBOL execution, which AAP 0.7.6 proves impossible in this environment across eight independently verified blockers: CBSTM03B is refused outright at :116 with 'executable program requested but PROCEDURE/ENTRY has USING clause', ORGANIZATION INDEXED is unsupported because the indexed file handler is disabled, and no Language Environment CEE* service exists. AAP 0.9.11 escalates the substitution for explicit user confirmation; it changes the provenance of the expected values and nothing else - twenty cases per program, field-for-field diffing and a diff count of zero across all twenty per module (gates G15 and G18) all stand. HOW THE CALL SCRIPT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN HELD IN JAVA: the sequence of CALLs below used to live in a Java switch over this file's case identifier, which meant the case file did not describe the one thing it asserts - a subroutine whose entire contract is a DD name plus a one-character operation code IS its call sequence. Renumbering this file would have silently given it a different script, and a twenty-first case would have thrown from a default arm. unitStimulus.operationScript now carries it, one entry per CALL in issue order, each declaring LK-M03B-DD, the 88-level operation code from app/cbl/CBSTM03B.cbl:103-108, and where applicable LK-M03B-KEY and LK-M03B-KEY-LN. Two caller idioms are declared explicitly because the source distinguishes them: status '00' is the MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC every real call site issues, and its ABSENCE carries the previous call's status forward - the only way to observe a fall-through exit that assigns nothing new; primesRecordArea true is the MOVE SPACES TO WS-M03B-FLDT that app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L350, :L745 and :L834 issue, and its ABSENCE is the omission at :L857-860 that makes 'at end of file the record area is returned unchanged' an assertion with content. Every expected area image below was derived from this script by reading CBSTM03B's rules, never by running the Java.
